title: First drive
brief:
The rover has just woken up on the surface of Mars. It is standing on the left-hand square of the top row, facing east. Three squares ahead of it, mission control has spotted an interesting rock sample.

Write a program that drives the rover east until it reaches the rock, and then collects the rock. The rover understands only four commands: `move()`, `turn_left()`, `pick_rock()` and `put_rock()`. Each command is a function call - the name of the function followed by a pair of parentheses.

All of your commands must go inside the main function, and every line inside `main()` must be indented by four spaces. The last two lines of the file start the program - leave them exactly as they are.

vocabulary.gloss: a self-contained block of code that performs one specific task. You define it once and can call it many times.
tell the computer to run (execute) that set of actions, by writing the name followed by brackets: `name()`.
the function where the program starts. It usually controls the program by calling other functions.
a round bracket `( )`. A function is always called with a pair of them, even when it needs no information: `move()`.
the spaces at the beginning of a line of code. In Python, indentation shows which lines belong inside a function, a loop or an if-statement.

starterCode:
from rover.marsrover import *

# File: first_drive.py
# --------------------
# Drive the rover to the rock sample and collect it.

def main():
    pass  # replace this line with your commands


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
hints: One `move()` moves the rover exactly one square in the direction it is facing.
The rock is three squares away, so you need three `move()` calls before `pick_rock()`.
reflect: What does it mean to call a function? Explain it in your own words, using one of the rover commands as an example.
solution:
from rover.marsrover import *

# File: first_drive.py
# --------------------
# Drive the rover to the rock sample and collect it.

def main():
    move()
    move()
    move()
    pick_rock()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
